facts.text: The project is the modified Panda-gym benchmark for evaluating skill-aware reinforcement-learning algorithms

The documented use is gym.make('PandaSkillAware-v3', render_mode='rgb_array', friction=1.0, mass=1.0) followed by reset() and step(action), which returns observation, reward, terminated, truncated and info
info['state'] is one of push, roll, pick and down
PandaSkillAware-v3 is registered with entry point skill_aware_panda_gym.envs:PandaPushEnv and max_episode_steps=50
PandaPushEnv is a RobotTaskEnv task environment
PandaPushEnv builds PyBullet with the requested render mode and renderer and a Panda robot in that simulation, with block_gripper=False and base_position [-0.6, 0.0, 0.0]
control_type selects end-effector control ('ee', the default) or joint control ('joints')
friction and mass are constructor arguments that default to 1.0
set_obs_friction_mass writes the mass to the object body with changeDynamics and the lateral friction to the table body
The task wrapper's defaults are distance_threshold 0.05, goal_xy_range 0.3, goal_z_range 0.11, obj_xy_range 0.3 and object_height 1.0
The environment constructs the task with the requested object_height and goal_z_range=0.0

get_state labels the object 'pick' when it is above 0.021 with no table contact and both finger contacts, 'roll' when it is above 0.021 otherwise, 'push' when it is between 0.019 and 0.21, and 'down' otherwise
PandaPushEnv.step applies the action, advances the simulation once, sets truncated=False, and returns the five-value Gymnasium result with info['state']
The installation requirements are gymnasium>=0.26, pybullet, numpy, scipy and panda-gym, with no serial, VISA or vendor-SDK dependency

determinism.notes: the fake's reset(seed=...) fixes the object and goal draws with Python's random.Random and its step is deterministic, so one seed repeats a trajectory on this package; the upstream reset is inherited from panda-gym's RobotTaskEnv, which is not in this clone and seeds numpy's generator, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the fake and upstream

gaps: analytic kinematics only: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, mass, actuator or sensor noise; the skill label comes from the stand-in's own geometric flags, not from PyBullet contact points
the clone exposes no simulation timestep, so timestep_ms is 0: the fake advances one transition per step and makes no claim about simulated time
the fake reproduces the registration's 50-step TimeLimit although the clone's own step always returns truncated=False
the action space is built by panda-gym's Panda class, an external dependency that is not in this clone: the fake's Box bounds and width are test data and were not compared with an installed upstream

the observation structure follows panda-gym's external RobotTaskEnv (a robot block, the task's object pose and velocity block, and the achieved and desired goals); its sizes are stand-in test data, not stated by this clone
the clone defines no reset of its own and seeds nothing: the fake seeds Python's random.Random while panda-gym's RobotTaskEnv uses numpy's generator
no rendering is modelled (render_mode is accepted and ignored), and snapshot/restore is not offered

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
